# Jubilees Chapter 43 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob learns Joseph lives; the descent to Egypt; Pharaoh blesses Jacob

---

**43:1** And when Jacob heard that Joseph was alive and that he was ruler over all Egypt, he was greatly moved in spirit. And he said: "It is enough; Joseph my son is yet alive. I will go and see him before I die."

**43:2** And Jacob arose with his sons and journeyed to Egypt. And they came to Goshen, and Joseph went up to meet his father Jacob.

**43:3** And Joseph fell upon his father's neck and wept greatly. And Jacob said: "Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, that thou art still alive."

**43:4** And Joseph brought his father and his brothers and set them before Pharaoh, and they bowed down before him.

**43:5** And Pharaoh said to Jacob: "How old art thou?" And Jacob said: "The days of my pilgrimage are one hundred and thirty years. Few and evil have been the days of my life, and they have not attained to the days of the years of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage."

**43:6** And Pharaoh blessed Jacob and all his sons, and Jacob and his sons ate bread before Pharaoh.

**43:7** And Joseph gave his father and his brothers a possession in the land of Egypt in Goshen, the best of the land. And he provided for them with food. And Jacob and his sons dwelt in Egypt in the land of Goshen.

**43:8** And the famine continued through all the land of Egypt and through all the land of Canaan. And Joseph gathered all the silver of the Egyptians and of the Canaanites for the grain which they bought.

**43:9** And all the Egyptians came to Joseph saying: "Give us bread, for our silver is spent." And Joseph said: "Give your cattle, and I will give you food for your cattle."

**43:10** And they brought their cattle to Joseph — horses and asses and oxen and sheep and goats — and Joseph gave them food. And that year he gathered all their cattle.

**43:11** And when the next year came, they came again and said: "We have nothing left but our bodies and our land. Take us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh."

**43:12** And Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, except the land of the priests, for the priests had a portion from Pharaoh. And Joseph made it an ordinance for all the land of Egypt to this day.

---

*EMET notes: Jacob's speech before Pharaoh (v.5) — "Few and evil have been the days of my life" — is one of the most poignant in the patriarchal narratives. Jubilees preserves it. The famine management material (vv.8-12) follows Genesis 47:13-26 closely, showing Joseph's shrewd consolidation of Pharaoh's economic power.*
